messages.subject: Shiny server permissions issue
messages.subject_clean: Shiny server permissions issue
messages.body_plain:
Okay, when run locally on my PC, my update data button (that runs an update_data.R script) functions fine. This polls the twitter search api for new data and updates a .Rdata file if there's new data. But, once I move it over to an AWS ubuntu image, the update data button errors out with a "cannot open connection" error. Try it out here... http://107.22.187.183:3838/minneapolis-fp-tweets/

I set up the server using the tutorial, so the shiny stuff is running as a user called 'shiny'. So my first thought was to change ownership of all of the /var/shiny-server/www/minneapolis-fp-tweets files to 'shiny'. This didn't work. I also gave r and x permissions to all users to the update_data.R script and the search.R script that it calls. That didn't do it either. I also made sure everybody had write permission to the .Rdata file that the script is supposed to update.

Code is here... https://github.com/corynissen/minneapolis-fp-tweets/tree/master/minneapolis-fp-tweets

Any ideas?

Thanks
Cory
messages.body_snippet: Okay, when run locally on my PC, my update data button (that runs an update_data.R script) functions fine. This polls the twitter search api for new data and updates a .Rdata file if there's new data.

messages.subject_clean: General Question: How do you test shiny apps?
messages.body_plain:
Here is a quick example using the example Height and Weight apllication on glimmer:

# A java binary titled selenium-server-standalone.jar needs to reside in /bin
# for startserver().
startServer()
remDr <- remoteDriver$new()
remDr$open()
remDr$navigate("http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/heightweight/")

# find the X variable DOM element
webElem <- remDr$findElement(using = "id", value = "x_var")

# check what is selected as default

webElem$getElementAttribute("value") # [1] "ageYear"

# change to x = Weight option
webElem <- remDr$findElement(value = "//option[@value = 'weightLb']")
webElem$clickElement() # app should change to x variable = weight

# change to x = Height
webElem <- remDr$findElement(value = "//option[@value = 'heightIn']")
webElem$clickElement() # app should change to x variable = weight

# seperate male and female values
webElem <- remDr$findElement(using = "id", value = "sex")
webElem$clickElement() # app should change to x variable = weight

# close server
remDr$closeServer()

messages.body_plain:
You never enter in shinyUI/shinyServer calls directly at the console (and you never source ui.R and server.R files). Instead you point Shiny at them by calling runApp() and passing in the directory where these files live. They need to be executed at particular times in the web application lifecycle so it's not something you can do from the console.

See http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#run-and-debug

In this particular example you can run:

shiny::runGist("https://gist.github.com/wch/4034323")

messages.subject_clean: Multiple Inputs Sharing an input variable name?
messages.body_plain:
I've got a UI function that looks like the code below.  I thought I could save a lot of headache in my server.r function by having conditional panels set input variables to different values (i.e. one conditional panel sets selectInput("x"....) to a series of values and another conditional panel may set selectInput("x" ...) to something different as shown below.

The problem I'm running into is that this does not work.  It just sets "x" to whatever the original value is.  Is there a better way to do this, or do I just have to create separate input variables for each and every case?

conditionalPanel(
                    condition = "input.selectedPanel == 'Purchase Metrics'",
                    selectInput("inputGranularity", "Select Date Granularity:", granularities),
                    selectInput("inputMetric", "Select Metric:", purchaseMetrics)
                ),
                conditionalPanel(
                    condition = "input.selectedPanel == 'Traffic Metrics'",
                    selectInput("inputGranularity", "Select Date Granularity:", granularities),
                    selectInput("inputMetric", "Select Metric:", trafficMetrics)
                ),
                conditionalPanel(
                    condition = "input.selectedPanel == 'Content Metrics'",
                    selectInput("inputGranularity", "Select Date Granularity:", granularitiesShort),
                    selectInput("inputMetric", "Select Metric:", contentMetrics)
                    #uiOutput("selectedElementInput")
                ),
                conditionalPanel(
                    condition = "input.selectedPanel == 'Campaign Metrics'",
                    selectInput("inputGranularity", "Select Date Granularity:", granularitiesShort),
                    selectInput("inputMetric", "Select Metric:", campaignMetrics),
                    selectInput("inputClassification", "Select Classification:", campaignClassifications)
                    #uiOutput("selectedElementInput")
                ),
                conditionalPanel(
                    condition = "input.selectedPanel == 'Product Metrics'",
                    selectInput("inputGranularity", "Select Date Granularity:", granularitiesShort),
                    selectInput("inputMetric", "Select Metric:", productMetrics),
                    selectInput("inputClassification", "Select Classification:", productClassifications)
                    #uiOutput("selectedElementInput")
                )
)

messages.subject: shiny-server, multiple users and heavy computations
messages.subject_clean: shiny-server, multiple users and heavy computations
messages.body_plain:
Hello again.

I am building tools that will be made public to many users. Let's say one of these tools provides an interface for a user to execute computations that takes R ~15-30 seconds to complete. If, say, 10 users all hit Go at about the same time in this proposed tool, is the 10th user going to wait ~150-300 seconds to get his/her results?

I can further-clarify my question if necessary. Basically, I am wondering if the computations will stack, or if shiny-server runs them independent of one another (in parallel).

Thanks again for this wonderful R library!

PS if they do stack, this becomes quite a large limitation... and my question becomes: "... is the only way around this to implement large-scale parallel processing R libraries? ... i.e., Rmpi

of ./configure && make from source, because it is likely that you
missed an optional dependency without noticing it. You need to read
the output from ./configure carefully.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9468164/problems-installing-r-on-linux-centos-6-2

compile R-devel from source on glimmer (although it is Ubuntu, you
should be able to see the problem of the png() device). Or just try my
build here: /home/yihui/repos/r-source/bin/R It will be great if you
can figure this out, because it has puzzled me for quite a while. My
best guess is pango headers were not installed.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: shiny-server, multiple users and heavy computations
messages.subject_clean: shiny-server, multiple users and heavy computations
messages.body_plain:
For each Shiny R process, the computations stack as you describe--this is an inevitable consequence of R being single-threaded.

The open source version of Shiny Server launches a single R process per app. The commercial version will allow you to configure multiple R processes per app; you could configure it to launch a new R process for each user if you wanted.

> Hello again.
>
> I am building tools that will be made public to many users. Let's say one of these tools provides an interface for a user to execute computations that takes R ~15-30 seconds to complete. If, say, 10 users all hit Go at about the same time in this proposed tool, is the 10th user going to wait ~150-300 seconds to get his/her results?
>
> I can further-clarify my question if necessary. Basically, I am wondering if the computations will stack, or if shiny-server runs them independent of one another (in parallel).
>
> Thanks again for this wonderful R library!

Here is functional code to make a variable number of plots based on the number of columns.  I suggest using this as a starting point, and adding small amounts of code until you pinpoint what exactly is breaking it.

server.r:
max_plots <- 100
library(shinyIncubator)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

sampletable=reactive({
if(input$go<1)
return()

x1=c(106:110, 21:25)
x2=c(101:105, 201:205)
x3=c(21:25, 31:35)
x4=c(51:60)
input$go
x=isolate(rbind(x1,x2,x3,x4))

x
})
  # Insert the right number of plot output objects into the web page
  output$plots <- renderUI({
    plot_output_list <- lapply(1:ncol(sampletable()), function(i) {

      plotname <- paste("plot", i, sep="")
      plotOutput(plotname, height = 280, width = 250)
    })

    # Convert the list to a tagList - this is necessary for the list of items
    # to display properly.
    do.call(tagList, plot_output_list)
  })

  # Call renderPlot for each one. Plots are only actually generated when they
  # are visible on the web page.
  for (i in 1:max_plots) {
    # Need local so that each item gets its own number. Without it, the value
    # of i in the renderPlot() will be the same across all instances, because
    # of when the expression is evaluated.
    local({
      my_i <- i
      plotname <- paste("plot", my_i, sep="")

      output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot({
        plot(sampletable()[,my_i], sampletable()[,my_i],
             xlim = c(min(sampletable()[,my_i]), max(sampletable()[,my_i])),
             ylim = c(min(sampletable()[,my_i]), max(sampletable()[,my_i])),
             main = "look at all those things"        )
      })
    })
  }
})

ui.r

library(shinyIncubator)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Dynamic number of plots"),

  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("n", "this isn't used, I used the ncol function instead, but feel free to move the slider for fun.", value=1, min=1, max=5),
  actionButton("go", "Update")
  ),

  mainPanel(
    # This is the dynamic UI for the plots
    uiOutput("plots")
  )
))

So I am running into some problems. So perhaps I should add some background into what I am trying to accomplish.

I am trying to import the following dataframe as a .csv file.

This is super simplified. But primarily I am trying to this up so that there is a file input to select the .csv file, then create a graph comparing Darkness to Mean.Diff for each unique Dark.Div value. It is important to set this up as a varying entity since there are some .csv files with 1,2,3 or 4 different Dark.Div values.

There seems to be an issue with the values being added using a fileInput instead of directly being written into the server.R file. The entire simplified server.R and ui.R is below.

Server.R

max_plots <- 100
library(shinyIncubator)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  inFile = reactive({

    if(input$go<1)
      return()

    x <- input$file1

    if (is.null(x) == TRUE){
      return(NULL)

    }

    x

  })
  # Insert the right number of plot output objects into the web page
  output$plots <- renderUI({

    x <- inFile()
    num.Div = length(unique(x$Dark.Div))

    plot_output_list <- lapply(1:num.Div, function(i) {

      plotname <- paste("plot", i, sep="")

      plotOutput(plotname, height = 280, width = 250)
    })

    # Convert the list to a tagList - this is necessary for the list of items
    # to display properly.
    do.call(tagList, plot_output_list)

  })

  # Call renderPlot for each one. Plots are only actually generated when they
  # are visible on the web page.
  for (i in 1:max_plots) {
    # Need local so that each item gets its own number. Without it, the value

    # of i in the renderPlot() will be the same across all instances, because
    # of when the expression is evaluated.
    local({
      my_i <- i
      plotname <- paste("plot", my_i, sep="")

      output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot({

        x <- inFile1
        xx <- x[which(x$Dark.Div == unique(x$Dark.Div)[i]),]

        plot(xx$Darkness, xx$Mean.Diff,
             xlim = c(min(xx$Darkness), max(xx$Darkness)),

             ylim = c(min(xx$Mean.Diff), max(xx$Mean.Diff)),

             main = "look at all those things"        )
      })
    })
  }
})

UI.R

library(shinyIncubator)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Dynamic number of plots"),

  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("n", "this isn't used, I used the ncol function instead, but feel free to move the slider for fun.", value=1, min=1, max=5),

    actionButton("go", "Update"),

    fileInput('file1', 'Choose CSV File', multiple = FALSE,
              accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain'))

  ),

  mainPanel(
    # This is the dynamic UI for the plots
    uiOutput("plots")
  )
))

Have you tested that the data is being read in correctly, and is accessible in the way that you try to use it?  Before worrying about a variable number of plots, do a simple read in and look at it with browser() inserted in the code somewhere downstream.

Next, if that checks out, I would throw in a browser() in the renderUI (be sure to put in an action button requirement in the renderUI as well, similar to my example, so it doesn't skip right to that before you load the data set) and go through it line by line, examine the objects created, to see at which part it konks out.  The error message hints to me that it may be that one of the objects either isn't actually the way you expect it to be, or that there is a syntax error when trying to refer to that object.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny is working great on VM but not on real RedHat Server
messages.subject_clean: Shiny is working great on VM but not on real RedHat Server
messages.body_plain:
The requirements for the machine totally depend on the applications you want to run. Our example apps, for instance, are very lightweight on the CPU and RAM, so we can host dozens of simultaneous users on these concurrently. Some apps we've seen require dozens of seconds or minutes for some update steps in the app -- for such apps, having any more than 1 concurrent user would likely be an unpleasant user experience. (Note that running multiple processes for a single Shiny App and controlling how many should be allowed on each process is a feature we'll be releasing shortly in Shiny Server Pro).

Similarly, the amount of RAM needed totally depends on a.) the amount of RAM you're loading up globally when the application starts, and b.) how much RAM each user session will be adding in their own scope.

Our best advice would be to test your app and see how it performs.

messages.subject: Dynamic Input Problems
messages.subject_clean: Dynamic Input Problems
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I've got an interesting issue with dynamic inputs.

I have a reactive function that updates a global data object.  I also have a dynamic input (using uiOuput/renderUI) as well as a plot that both call that reactive function and rely on the global object that gets updated.  The plot works fine and the dynamic input works fine, however when the plot has to rely on the dynamic input, it doesn't work.  I think it's a problem because the plot is getting generated before the dynamic UI is finished generating, and the plot doesn't get any data since the plot relies on the dynamic UI.

Anyways, here's an example of the server.r code:

Here's the data update part.  Everything works if I use the yellow line.  However, it breaks if I use the green line (which relies on the input$inputContentSelectItems)

getData<-reactive({
        dataUpdate()
        rsid<-input$RSID

        if(input$selectedPanel=="Content Metrics"){
            selectedDateGran<-input$inputContentGranularity
            selectedMetric<-input$inputContentMetric
            #selectedColumn<-7
            selectedColumn<-which(names(allData[[rsid]][["contentMetrics"]][["prop1"]][[selectedMetric]][[selectedDateGran]]) == as.character(input$inputContentSelectItems))

            dataMat<-allData[[rsid]][["contentMetrics"]][["prop1"]][[selectedMetric]][[selectedDateGran]]
            if(length(dataMat$Day)==0){dataMat$Day<-1}
            dataMat$DateFormat<-as.Date(paste(dataMat$Month,"/",dataMat$Day,"/",dataMat$Year,sep=""  ),format="%m/%d/%Y")
            datesVec<-as.Date(as.character(dataMat$DateFormat))
            dataVec<-as.numeric(as.character(dataMat[,selectedColumn]))
        }

       list(datesVec,dataVec,selectedMetric,selectedDateGran)
})

Here's the plot output.  You can see that the plotting function relies on the reactive function output as well as some inputs.

output$anomolyContentPlot = renderPlot({
        dataUpdate()
        temp<-getData()

        datesVec<-temp[[1]]
        dataVec<-temp[[2]]

        dataVec
        metricName1<-temp[[3]]
        graphDateGranularity<-temp[[4]]

        meanSelection1<-as.numeric(input$modelOption1)
        meanSelection2<-as.numeric(input$modelOption2)
        stdevs<-as.numeric(input$stdevs)
        graphStartDate<-as.Date(input$inputDates[[1]])
        graphEndDate<-as.Date(input$inputDates[[2]])

        s.p<-as.numeric(input$srma)
        l.p<-as.numeric(input$lrma)
        e.p<-as.numeric(input$erma)

        plotAnomolies(meanSelection1,
            meanSelection2,
            stdevs,
            datesVec,
            dataVec,
            graphStartDate,
            graphEndDate,
            s.p,
            l.p,
            e.p,
            myMetricName=metricName1,
            graphDateGranularity=graphDateGranularity)
    })

messages.subject: Re: sidebars & sliders - questiions
messages.subject_clean: sidebars & sliders - questiions
messages.body_plain:
I believe both questions were asked in this group.
1) Can be done with conditional panels. The sidebar panel stays the same, but elements turn visible when a specific tab panel active. Items that are not placed inside conditional panel would be shared across all tabs. For this you need to specify JavaScript condition like "input.tabset_id == 'tabPanel_value' ". e.g. UI.R:
 sidebarPanel
        (
            textInput("sharedText", "Shared textbox","")
            # insert other controls shared across tabs

            conditionalPanel # Elements displayed when tab with value "First" active
            (
                condition = "input.tabMain == 'First'"
                #... insert controls you need to show when First tab active
            ),
            conditionalPanel # Elements displayed when tab with value "Second" active
            (
                condition = "input.tabMain == 'Second'"
                #... insert controls you need to show when Second tab active
            )
        ),
        mainPanel
        (
            tabsetPanel
            (
                id = "tabMain",
                tabPanel
                (
                     title = "first",
                     value = "First"

messages.body_plain:
I built R-trunk from source, and get the same error. But png(type="cairo") works fine.

Even though png() has a default of type=c("cairo", "cairo-png", "Xlib", "quartz"), it doesn't actually use "cairo" as the default, because of this line:
 if(missing(type)) type <- getOption("bitmapType")

So it actually uses the value of getOption("bitmapType"). On the normal R installation, this returns:
> getOption("bitmapType")
[1] "cairo"

But on the version built from source:
> getOption("bitmapType")
[1] "Xlib"

Now, it appears that the bitmapType option gets set when grDevices is loaded:
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/518237f9eaf95fb477346e4b7c04aed7a2ef7901/src/library/grDevices/R/zzz.R#L32

list(bitmapType = if(capabilities("aqua")) "quartz"

else if(.Call(C_cairoProps, 2L)) "cairo" else "Xlib")

For some reason this returns FALSE on my R-trunk built from source:
   .Call(grDevices:::C_cairoProps, 2L) # FALSE
That value is probably not right, considering that I can create PNG graphics just fine with png(type="cairo").

In the installed R 2.15.3 on Glimmer, the corresponding call returns TRUE
   .Call(grDevices:::cairoProps, 2L) # TRUE

And if you dig deeper into the C code, it looks like FALSE value does have something to do with Pango, via HAVE_PANGOCAIRO:
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/518237f9eaf95fb477346e4b7c04aed7a2ef7901/src/library/grDevices/R/zzz.R#L33

I don't see anywhere in the R source where HAVE_PANGOCAIRO is set to 1, so I'm not really sure what to make of this. Perhaps it's supposed to be set in a header from Pango?

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

I'm trying to do the same thing as Sam (Launch a shiny app from inside an RStudio Server instance) and I'm just having a little trouble with the workaround you suggested. Basically, I wrote  something like this:

runApp("myApp",launch.browser=F)
browseURL("http://myserver:8100")

I find that my code does not progress to the browseURL line because the shiny app is running and I assume that it will not execute that line until the shiny app has terminated. Is there some special way or place that I should be putting the browseURL() bit so that my browser is launched with the correct URL?

Aside, I see that the hostname "localhost" is hard-coded in the runApp function and assume that it would be a quick fix to just add that hostname as an argument to the runApp function. Are there reasons (security-related perhaps?) that this is a bad idea?

Thanks for your help!

Rob

I do not see cairopango on glimmer:

$ pkg-config --list-all | grep cairo
cairo-xcb             cairo-xcb - XCB surface backend for cairo graphics library
cairo-gobject         cairo-gobject - gobject functions for cairo
graphics library
cairo-ps              cairo-ps - PostScript surface backend for cairo
graphics library
cairo-pdf             cairo-pdf - PDF surface backend for cairo graphics library
cairo-xlib            cairo-xlib - Xlib surface backend for cairo
graphics library
cairo-xcb-shm         cairo-xcb-shm - XCB/SHM functions for cairo
graphics library
cairo-fc              cairo-fc - Fontconfig font backend for cairo
graphics library
cairo-xlib-xrender    cairo-xlib-xrender - Xlib Xrender surface
backend for cairo graphics library
cairo                 cairo - Multi-platform 2D graphics library
cairo-png             cairo-png - PNG functions for cairo graphics library
cairo-ft              cairo-ft - FreeType font backend for cairo
graphics library
cairo-svg             cairo-svg - SVG surface backend for cairo graphics library

$ pkg-config --list-all | grep pango

Under Ubuntu, it is easy to install the dependencies required for
building a package from source, e.g. for R, you can

  sudo apt-get build-dep r-base-dev

I think what is missing on glimmer is libpango1.0-dev, as you will
find out when running apt-get build-dep.

I'm not sure what is the equivalent command for Red Hat, though.
Building R from source is tricky without something like apt-get
build-dep.

Regards,
Yihui
--

>

Ah, good call. I was doing this:
$ pkg-config --exists pangocairo
$ echo $?
1

But I thought 1 meant true -- I forgot that in shell scripts, 0 is success and other values are failure.

>
> Under Ubuntu, it is easy to install the dependencies required for
> building a package from source, e.g. for R, you can
>
>   sudo apt-get build-dep r-base-dev
>
> I think what is missing on glimmer is libpango1.0-dev, as you will
> find out when running apt-get build-dep.

It looks like we had run `sudo apt-get build-dep r-base`, but that was several months ago, and it must not have included libpango1.0-dev back then.

Yes, it appears that installing pango and re-running configure and make does the trick. On Ubuntu:
  apt-get install libpango1.0-dev

So now building R-trunk in Glimmer/Spark should result in png() just working.

> I'm not sure what is the equivalent command for Red Hat, though.
> Building R from source is tricky without something like apt-get
> build-dep.

Thanks!
-Winston

messages.subject: simple example of dynamic drop down list--thanks to earlier posts and tutorial
messages.subject_clean: simple example of dynamic drop down list--thanks to earlier posts and tutorial
messages.body_plain:
This is related to the question posed by Cindy Hart but not a solution to her questions.  I built a toy example that illustrates a dynamically populated drop down list and post it here to help other new users learn more about dynamic tools in shiny.  I am interested in getting dynamic controls specific to tabs, will follow up the other string for that.

The problem is motivated by an analysis of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services payment data set, which consists of ~160,000 payment records from 2011, organized by diagnostic related group (DRG); state; and hospital within state.

I want to allow the user to select a DRG and a state in drop down lists in the UI (these lists do not need to be defined dynamically).  Then given this information, populate a third drop down list of hospitals for the specific state and DRG for further analysis.  I create the list of hospital names for each state once in the global code and just select the correct hospital list given the state name.    I think this may be faster than creating the list on the fly but I did not tests.

The example creates summaries of data, the actual application has a set of scatter plot--the hard part for me was getting the dynamic drop down list to work.

Code posted on https://gist.github.com/klittle314/6161538

messages.subject_clean: How to merge a "static dataframe" and a "reactive dataframe"
messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody,

I have a doubt about how to merge a "static dataframe" and a "reactive dataframe". I am getting my data from a ODBC passing input values from ui.R into the WHERE clause, so this way I have a "reactive dataframe" which is refreshed whenever I change the input settings (in this case they are dates).

Let's say my "reactive dataframe" has 4 variables (v1, v2, v3, v4) where v1 and v2 are factors which could have NA values. Let's say my "static dataframe" contains two columns called v1 and v2 (of the same length) which are the lists of all posible values (levels) for factors v1 and v2, and an extra column called w1.

What I would like to do is to add to my "reactive dataframe"  the values from the column w1 according to values of v1 and v2. For example:

Reactive dataframe:

v1   v2   v3    v4
A    A     5      01-01-13
A    A     10    03-01-13
B           15    03 -01-13
B    A     6      04 -01-13
....

Static dataframe:

v1   v2   w1
A    A     Bart
A    B     Lisa
B    A     Homer
B    B     Marge

The resulting dataframe I'd like to get:

v1   v2   v3    v4                w1
A    A     5      01-01-13     Bart
A    A     10    03-01-13     Bart
B           15    03 -01-13
B    A      6     04 -01-13    Homer
...

I have tried to get it with merge() function but it seems to be a recursion problem because I get this error:

Error : evaluation nested too deeply: infinite recursion / options(expressions=)?

I provide a basic code to illustrate the problem. Any help is appreciated.

Thanks in advance.
Igor

ui.R ========================================================================

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

 sidebarPanel(

    # The input fields for starting and ending dates

    textInput("dateSTA","Starting date (dd-mm-yy)", '01-01-13'),
    textInput("dateEND","Ending date(dd-mm-yy)", '10-01-13'),

),

 mainPanel(

    tableOutput("outputtable")

  )

  )
)

server.R ========================================================================

library(shiny)

# Here I create a new table from a csv file on my disk
external_table<-read.csv(file="mypath", options)

# Here I connect with my database
library(RODBC)
mychannel<-odbcConnect("myDB", uid = "myui", pwd = "mypwd", believeNRows=FALSE)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

 # Here I get a table from a query againts my database

 mytable<-reactive({ sqlQuery(conexion, paste('

SELECT

v1, v2, v3, v4

FROM adatabasetable

WHERE var4 BETWEEN \'',input$dateSTA,'\' AND \'',input$dateEND,'\'

'))

})

  # Then I merge both tables this way (I think this is the wrong part of my code) and refresh mytable

 mytable<-reactive({ merge(mytable(), external_table, all.x=TRUE) })

# Then I print  mytable in the output

  output$outputtable<- renderTable({

as.data.frame(mytable())

  })

})

messages.subject: checking for more than just server.R's timestamp
messages.subject_clean: checking for more than just server.R's timestamp
messages.body_plain:
I have a rapidly growing application that I've begun to split up into separate source .R files, loaded into server.R with source(..., local=T).  This seems the best way to manage burgeoning complexity.

Of course, now when I update those files, I have to also "touch" server.R to get the server to reload the sources.  I see the function in shiny.R that controls this behavior, and it seems it could easily be configured to look for other .R files (perhaps in a certain configurable directory) or any file specified by a matching glob string, and to take the most recent modified time over all these files, rather than just the mtime of server.R

Are there objections/concerns with such behavior?  I'm happy to supply the first iteration of a patch, but don't want to waste time if the "vision" is going elsewhere.

Thanks,
-Aaron

messages.body_plain:
I suspect that when you compiled R, it didn't have any cairo support at all - this is slightly different from the issue on a separate thread, where, on Ubuntu, the compiled R had cairo support but not pango, and was confused about whether it could output cairo graphics.

I think the next thing to try is to install the development libraries for cairo and pango, then re-compile R. This should install the development libraries for both:
  sudo yum install pango-devel

Then go to your R source directory and do something like this to rebuild it (but if you used a different procedure before, do that instead):
  make distclean
  ./configure
  make

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: How to merge a "static dataframe" and a "reactive dataframe"
messages.subject_clean: How to merge a "static dataframe" and a "reactive dataframe"
messages.body_plain:
This is caused because both your functions are called mytable and the infinite recursion should be clear from this line:

 mytable<-reactive({ merge(mytable(), external_table, all.x=TRUE) })

You simply need to have

mytable <-reactive({ do SQL stuff here })
mytable2 <-reactive({merge(mytable(), external_table, all.x=TRUE)  })

And then call mytable2() in your output. When input changes, it will cause mytable() to reactivate, which will cause mytable2() to reactivate, which will cause output to change.

> mine=mytable()
> this=merge(mine, external_table, all.x=TRUE)
> this
> })

Let's say my "static dataframe" contains two columns called v1 and v2 (of the same length) which are the lists of all posible values (levels) for factors v1 and v2, and an extra column called w1.

messages.subject: Shiny Lag Issue, Too Many Reactives?
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Lag Issue, Too Many Reactives?
messages.body_plain:
Hey all,

I have been trying to make my app run more efficiently- because to my surprise, it can be a bit lagged on my 10gb mac desktop.  I investigated the memory usage on the machine after restarting, as the program ran and looked to see when it became sluggish responding to the user input.  I did not notice it ever having issues with ram, it almost always had at least 7gb free to work with, regardless of how sluggish it was/wasn't.

I then decided to see which tabs it became sluggish after completing- I should probably describe the overall structure of my app.  The app is initially divided into many 6 tabs, all of which are page with sidebars.  The first tab is a initiation tab, where all the options are set for the analysis ahead, and after filling in all the fields, the analysis is run.  The five additional tabs are to generate and view figures and tables from the results of the analysis run on the first tab.  In the first tab, one of the fields is a 'select columns', not dissimilar from Winston's example.  This is the area in which I test the lag of checkbox clicking, initially, it is very rapid and keeps up with how fast I can click the buttons.

The first tab has ~10 inputs, which are put into reactives and isolated by one of several action buttons.  After running the analysis itself, the checkboxes are only slightly more lagged, barely noticeable.
The second tab generates a simple plot, and there are only 3 inputs, which are put into reactives and isolated with an action button.  after generating a plot, there is no noticeable difference from the prior step.
The third tab and the fourth tab are similar, in that they have ~10 inputs each, which are turned into isolated reactives, and generate a plot and a table, respectively.  It is after generating either of these that the app becomes slow to respond to user input.
The fifth tab itself has only 2 inputs, each turned into an isolated reactive, but has 5 tabs, each of which have 3 tables.  There was no lag after generating these tables.
The sixth tab generates between 2 and 40 plots, but it is an optional analysis which takes a while to run, so I haven't tested it yet.

So my question is, has anyone else experienced shiny being slow to respond to your input after generating ~20-30 reactives?  Or do you think it may be something else?

Thanks again,
Mike

messages.subject_clean: Shiny server / ggplot2 error?
messages.body_plain:
Sorry to hear that it didn't work for you. I _think_ the key is to compile R with cairo development libraries -- when you run ./configure, it will probably report at the console (and somewhere in config.log) whether it finds them. For your version of CentOS, there may be other packages besides pango-devel and cairo-devel that are needed in order to compile R with cairo support, but I'm not sure what else is required.

If you can find R 3.0.1 packages for your version of CentOS, that would probably be much easier.

-Winston

Is there a way to adjust the slider bar so that it's on a log scale or something?  Ideally, for my project the leftmost value would be like .65, the middle value .95, and the far right value be .999 and still have continuous values in between.

Do I need to use a transformation function so that the value is really 0 to 1, but it translates to whatever input I need?  If so, how can I get the output to show .65 to .999 even though the value of the slider bar itself is 0 to 1?

messages.subject: Re: multiple text inputs
messages.subject_clean: multiple text inputs
messages.body_plain:
That means you have this somewhere:
  reactive(function() {
    ...
  })

That's how the first versions of Shiny wanted reactive() to work. In recent versions of Shiny, the function() part is deprecated, so this is what you should use:
  reactive({
    ...
  })

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Lag Issue, Too Many Reactives?
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Lag Issue, Too Many Reactives?
messages.body_plain:
It's unlikely the number of reactives would slow things down--the overhead of reactive execution is fairly low and cost no CPU when they are not invalidated.

Would it be possible to share your code?

On Wednesday, August 7, 2013, Mike C wrote:

> Hey all,
>
> I have been trying to make my app run more efficiently- because to my surprise, it can be a bit lagged on my 10gb mac desktop.  I investigated the memory usage on the machine after restarting, as the program ran and looked to see when it became sluggish responding to the user input.  I did not notice it ever having issues with ram, it almost always had at least 7gb free to work with, regardless of how sluggish it was/wasn't.
>
> I then decided to see which tabs it became sluggish after completing- I should probably describe the overall structure of my app.  The app is initially divided into many 6 tabs, all of which are page with sidebars.  The first tab is a initiation tab, where all the options are set for the analysis ahead, and after filling in all the fields, the analysis is run.  The five additional tabs are to generate and view figures and tables from the results of the analysis run on the first tab.  In the first tab, one of the fields is a 'select columns', not dissimilar from Winston's example.  This is the area in which I test the lag of checkbox clicking, initially, it is very rapid and keeps up with how fast I can click the buttons.
>
> The first tab has ~10 inputs, which are put into reactives and isolated by one of several action buttons.  After running the analysis itself, the checkboxes are only slightly more lagged, barely noticeable.
> The second tab generates a simple plot, and there are only 3 inputs, which are put into reactives and isolated with an action button.  after generating a plot, there is no noticeable difference from the prior step.
> The third tab and the fourth tab are similar, in that they have ~10 inputs each, which are turned into isolated reactives, and generate a plot and a table, respectively.  It is after generating either of these that the app becomes slow to respond to user input.
> The fifth tab itself has only 2 inputs, each turned into an isolated reactive, but has 5 tabs, each of which have 3 tables.  There was no lag after generating these tables.
> The sixth tab generates between 2 and 40 plots, but it is an optional analysis which takes a while to run, so I haven't tested it yet.
>
> So my question is, has anyone else experienced shiny being slow to respond to your input after generating ~20-30 reactives?  Or do you think it may be something else?
>
> Thanks again,
> Mike
>

messages.subject: Re: log scale on slider input?
messages.subject_clean: log scale on slider input?
messages.body_plain:
The jslider widget that the sliderInput uses is capable of displaying arbitrary labels on each tick, but Shiny's R and Javascript code that wraps up the jslider doesn't expose all of the functionality that would be needed.

See example here:
  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winstontest/slider-labels/
  https://github.com/wch/testapp/tree/master/slider-labels

The labels are arbitrary, and are manually set so they appear logarithmic; the actual values are shown on top. Probably for your case, you'd want to hide the value on top or make it display a transformed value.

If you're curious about what jslider can do, see the last example here - it uses times for labels and has a transformation function to show the time for the labels below, and for the value above the slider.
  http://egorkhmelev.github.io/jslider/

-Winston

messages.subject: (optional) download of an output
messages.subject_clean: (optional) download of an output
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

A common use of a shiny application, given the user's inputs, is run an isolated function, print the result and give an option to download the result.
Along with the printed output (a table, for example :) ), I would like a conditional "download" button to appear for the user for optional download of the result (as .CSV file).

On the server script I have one reactive function, with isolated part, and a download handler, which looks something like this:

library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output){
  output$table <- renderTable({
    if (input$goButton == 0)
      return()
    input$goButton
    table <- isolate({ ...some function...  return(result)})
    return(table)
  })
  output$downloadtable <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {paste('myoutput-', Sys.Date(), '.csv', sep='')},
    content = function(file) {if (input$goButton != 0) write.csv(output$table, file) else return()})
})

The UI.r has sidebar for inputs and a submit button and should reveal a "download" button after running the main function:

library(shiny)
shinyUI(
  pageWithSidebar(
    sidebarPanel(

     ...some inputs...

    conditionalPanel(condition="output.table",
                       downloadButton(outputId="downloadtable", label = "Download file"))
    ),

    mainPanel(
      h4("Results:"),
      tableOutput(outputId="table")
    )
    )
  )

However, running the app as above gives an error:

Reading objects from shinyoutput object not allowed.

Any Ideas for a workaround?
Or, What would you suggest to be the best practice script for downloading the results of an app...? (with the conditional "download" Button etc. as described)

Thanks!
Shay.

I investigated the memory usage on the machine after restarting, as the program ran and looked to see when it became sluggish responding to the user input.  I did not notice it ever having issues with ram, it almost always had at least 7gb free to work with, regardless of how sluggish it was/wasn't.
>
> I then decided to see which tabs it became sluggish after completing- I should probably describe the overall structure of my app.  The app is initially divided into many 6 tabs, all of which are page with sidebars. You should be calling write.csv on the data.frame, not the output object. To avoid calculating your table twice, put your data creation into a reactive function and then call it from each function.

shinyServer(function(input, output){

makeTable <-reactive({ #do data operations)}

output$table <- renderTable({

    if (input$goButton == 0)
      return()
    input$goButton

    table <- isolate({ makeTable())})

    return(table)
  })
  output$downloadtable <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {paste('myoutput-', Sys.Date(), '.csv', sep='')},

    content = function(file) {if (input$goButton != 0) write.csv(makeTable(), file) else return()})
})

Hi!

I love the Shiny App framework and am currently evaluating it for my own work. In order to do that I would like to build 2 small Shiny Apps to see whether they fit my needs. As I don't have enough time to do it myself, I am looking for a knowledgeable Shiny App developer who can build this for me.

Please find some more details below. I very much look forward to your replies!

And to the Shiny App team: Awesome stuff and keep up the great work! :)

Thanks, Ignacio

----------------------------

General description (I'm happy to share more details on request)

I would like to build 2 Shiny Apps that are able to

1) send a request to a REST web service
2) receive the resulting data from that request in the JSON format
3) create visualizations based on these data

Shiny app 1: Bar chart with 5 filter controls
Shiny app 2: 2 tables in tabs with 3 controls

Payment: USD 100-200 (ideally via Elance.com; alternatively via some other freelancer site)

Start date: Immediately

messages.subject: Caching Issue with googleVis, RPostgreSQL, and Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Caching Issue with googleVis, RPostgreSQL, and Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a Shiny dashboard of business metrics using plots from the googleVis package. The data that googleVis plots comes from a query stored in my server.R file; it is simply

drv <- dbDriver("PostgreSQL")

con <- dbConnect(drv, dbname="", user="", password="", port="", host="")
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "select * from mytable")
mydata <- fetch(rs, n=-1)
dbDisconnect(con)

When I start the Shiny server and open up the app for the first time, the query takes a brief moment to run and, upon finishing, Shiny displays the googleVis plots. If I decide to close the app and reopen it some other time, for some reason the app displays the plots instantaneously as if the query did not execute. Sure enough, the plots show the same old data as the first time the app was opened, implying that the query did not run.

Is this a behavior of Shiny where it chooses to cache the results of the query and display it upon future openings (without running the query again) or is this more along the lines of some RPostgreSQL feature? When this dashboard was created months ago, Shiny did not exhibit this behavior; the query would always take a moment to run before Shiny displays the plots. This is a recent behavior, leading me to believe it has something to do with Shiny.

Thanks for your help!

messages.subject: <hr> tag throws error in htmlEscape
messages.subject_clean: <hr> tag throws error in htmlEscape
messages.body_plain:
An <hr> tag in my shiny app causes an error in shiny:::htmlEscape:
the text arg in the htmlEscape call has the value character(0).
I can prevent the error by fixing htmlEscape, adding this code:
     if(length(text)==0)   text = ""
then using assignInNamespace(ns="shiny", x="htmlEscape", ...)
to place the fixed code for htmlEscape into the namespace;
then the error goes away.

Obviously not a satisfactory solution, so I'm currently doing without <hr>,
not a big sacrifice.
But the problem may show up with other tags.
It's a very easy fix.

-Roger

messages.body_plain:
It took me a couple of days of debugging to figure this out, so I wanted to bring it up in case anyone else ran into a similar issue. I'm on the latest CRAN release of Shiny (version .6?).

It appears that passing a zero-length logical to updateCheckboxInput causes the Shiny interface to more or less freeze up (or at least act in a very strange manner, updating some parts of the page but not others).  Obviously there are very few situations where you'd want to pass a zero-length logical to a checkbox, but accidents happen, and it would be helpful if an error were thrown indicating the problem.

This line causes the problem to occur whenever I insert it.  Adding It seems to affect random (or possibly all) objects on the page, not just those connected to the checkbox via reactive relationships.

updateCheckboxInput(session, "checkboxControlName", value=logical(0))

Otherwise, Shiny's been everything I could have asked for!  Thanks for a great product.

messages.subject: Re: Custom Shiny input/output binding
messages.subject_clean: Custom Shiny input/output binding
messages.body_plain:
There are several invalid things about these three lines of code.

A)
   BSub<-reactiveValues({input$blocksubj})
   output$d3io <- reactive({ShinyICs[BSub,]})
B)
   ShinyICs[BSub,]<-reactiveValuesToList({input$d3io})

reactiveValues doesn't take an expression, it takes name-value pairs.
You can't subset ShinyICs by a reactiveValues object, it would have to be something off of a reactiveValues object. I don't think that's what you mean either though.
You can't call reactiveValuesToList() on input$d3io, as the latter is not a "reactive values" object.
Here's one possibility for what you meant instead:

A)
   BSub<-reactive({input$blocksubj})
   output$d3io <- reactive({ShinyICs[BSub(),]})
B)
   ShinyICs[BSub,]<-input$d3io # I actually have no idea what you mean here

messages.subject: Re: Accessing dataset one has uploaded
messages.subject_clean: Accessing dataset one has uploaded
messages.body_plain:
I think the problem is that in your renderPlot, you're using read.csv(), but not saving the returned value anywhere.

You're probably better of using a reactive expression to load the file, instead of loading it twice. Something like this:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  inData <- reactive({
    inFile <- input$dataset
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
  })

  output$contents <- renderTable({
    inData()
  })

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    plot(inData())
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: Markdown in shiny

messages.body_plain:
For dynamics in your UI you can use renderUI

In server.R you have something like:

output$somename <- renderUI({
   includeMarkdown(input$file.name <http://file.name>)
})

Then in ui.R include:

uiOutput("some.name <http://some.name>")

messages.subject: Re: NULL being printed during reactive transition of inputs - possible to skip output?
messages.subject_clean: NULL being printed during reactive transition of inputs - possible to skip output?
messages.body_plain:
Oh, it might be because renderPrint, which tries to display the returned value as it would be if it were returned at the R console. That is, if the object has a visible flag, it would call print() on it; if not, it won't.

You can avoid this by using return(invisible()) instead of just return().

To illustrate, this is what happens at the R console:

f <- function() { return() }
f()
# NULL

g <- function() { return(invisible()) }
g()
# <no output>

If you want to know more about the visible flag, see ?withVisible.

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
With part B, I just wanted to return an array to the dataframe. It seemed that it would be just as easy to send the entire row to the Shiny client, and then send back to the server the same array with only one element changed. However, if returning a 70-item json array as both output and input isn't possible, then I could input a value and dataframe cell reference (i.e. the column index since the row index is BSub()).

On Wed, Aug 14, 2013 at 9:59 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> There are several invalid things about these three lines of code.
>
> A)
>    BSub<-reactiveValues({input$blocksubj})
>    output$d3io <- reactive({ShinyICs[BSub,]})
> B)
>    ShinyICs[BSub,]<-reactiveValuesToList({input$d3io})
>
> reactiveValues doesn't take an expression, it takes name-value pairs.
> You can't subset ShinyICs by a reactiveValues object, it would have to be something off of a reactiveValues object. I don't think that's what you mean either though.
> You can't call reactiveValuesToList() on input$d3io, as the latter is not a "reactive values" object.
> Here's one possibility for what you meant instead:
>
> A)
>    BSub<-reactive({input$blocksubj})
>    output$d3io <- reactive({ShinyICs[BSub(),]})
> B)
>    ShinyICs[BSub,]<-input$d3io # I actually have no idea what you mean here
>
>
>

> > Hi, Joe. Thanks for taking a look at this.
> > I tried in desperation to use isolate. I probably shouldn't use isolate at all.

> >    output$d3io <- reactive({ShinyICs[BSub,]})
> > B)
> >    ShinyICs[BSub,]<-reactiveValuesToList({input$d3io})
> >
> > The message (an array) should only go to the client when there is A) input$blocksubj
> > The message should return to the server only when there is B) input$d3io

> > Thanks!!

> >

> > > I noticed that in your output$d3io reactive, you read input$d3io three times, once with isolate() and twice without. What exactly are you trying to do here?
> > >
> > >
> > > On Tue, Aug 13, 2013 at 4:54 AM, Ryan Mears <rme...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > The problem with the logic of the Shiny bindings pertains to the update function on line 188 of d3widget.js and the output$d3io in server.R
> > > > The input and output bindings begin to oscillate between conflicting input and output messages after more than one selection has been made from the drop-down menu.
> > > >
> > > >

messages.body_plain:
Hi all, I would like to know if it's possible to serve content with something like an "r servlet" or a shiny server (here I mean server.R, not the node.js server that the subject refers to) but without the ui part. That is, a generic abstraction to handle http request/response. This way the shiny server (here I mean the node.js one) could be an alternative to rook, rapache or fastrweb. For example sometimes I would like to serve a jsonified dataframe directly to a node.js app that interacts with r through a web service hosted in a shiny server (the same I would do with, say, rook). I prefer the web service alternative to rserve plus rio.js or rserve-client.js.

Regards
--
Carlos

> > > Hey all,

> > > I have been trying to make my app run more efficiently- because to my surprise, it can be a bit lagged on my 10gb mac desktop.  I investigated the memory usage on the machine after restarting, as the program ran and looked to see when it became sluggish responding to the user input.  I did not notice it ever having issues with ram, it almost always had at least 7gb free to work with, regardless of how sluggish it was/wasn't.
> > >
> > > I then decided to see which tabs it became sluggish after completing- I should probably describe the overall structure of my app.  The app is initially divided into many 6 tabs, all of which are page with sidebars.  The first tab is a initiation tab, where all the options are set for the analysis ahead, and after filling in all the fields, the analysis is run.  The five additional tabs are to generate and view figures and tables from the results of the analysis run on the first tab.  In the first tab, one of the fields is a 'select columns', not dissimilar from Winston's example.  This is the area in which I test the lag of checkbox clicking, initially, it is very rapid and keeps up with how fast I can click the buttons.
> > >
> > > The first tab has ~10 inputs, which are put into reactives and isolated by one of several action buttons.  After running the analysis itself, the checkboxes are only slightly more lagged, barely noticeable.
> > > The second tab generates a simple plot, and there are only 3 inputs, which are put into reactives and isolated with an action button.  after generating a plot, there is no noticeable difference from the prior step.
> > > The third tab and the fourth tab are similar, in that they have ~10 inputs each, which are turned into isolated reactives, and generate a plot and a table, respectively.  It is after generating either of these that the app becomes slow to respond to user input.
> > > The fifth tab itself has only 2 inputs, each turned into an isolated reactive, but has 5 tabs, each of which have 3 tables.  There was no lag after generating these tables.
> > > The sixth tab generates between 2 and 40 plots, but it is an optional analysis which takes a while to run, so I haven't tested it yet.
> > >
> > > So my question is, has anyone else experienced shiny being slow to respond to your input after generating ~20-30 reactives?  Or do you think it may be something else?
> > >

messages.subject: Re: Shiny bug with rCharts? Attempt to apply non-function
messages.subject_clean: Shiny bug with rCharts? Attempt to apply non-function
messages.body_plain:
This error is occurring since renderChart2 is expecting an object belonging to an rCharts class. You might be able to rewrite the server side function such that renderChart2 is called only when the inputs defining the chart have been specified. A quick hack to resolve this within the code you have is to return an empty rChart instead of invisible. So essentially, modify the return(invisible()) statements in your code to return(rCharts$new()). This should not have any undesirable side effects since an empty chart wont print anything.

Hope this helps.

Ok, great!  I think I know what is going on.  My sample code relied upon the "readLines" command which inherently breaks different lines of code into different values of a vector or list.  However, the way shiny is handling it is as if each the entire block of code is one text block.  All I need to do is txt <- unlist(strsplit(txt, split="\n")).

Perfect!
Thanks man,
Francis

> > This error is occurring since renderChart2 is expecting an object belonging to an rCharts class. You might be able to rewrite the server side function such that renderChart2 is called only when the inputs defining the chart have been specified. A quick hack to resolve this within the code you have is to return an empty rChart instead of invisible. messages.subject: Re: How to show that Shiny is busy (or loading) when changing tab panels?
messages.subject_clean: How to show that Shiny is busy (or loading) when changing tab panels?
messages.body_plain:
The shiny-incubator package <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator> now has a progress indicator, see ?withProgress. Perhaps that would do the trick?

On Fri, Aug 16, 2013 at 12:14 PM, Jonathan Baik <jonn...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I posted this question on StackOverflow, and I am sorry for cross posting questions between different sites. I thought that I may receive better answers if I posted here.
>
> Link to SO question <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/18237987/show-that-shiny-is-busy-or-loading-when-changing-tab-panels> and copy pasted below. If there is a solution, feel free to post it as an answer on SO as well!
>
>
>
> I am working on making a web app with Shiny, and some of the R commands that I am executing take minutes to complete. I found that I need to provide the user with some indication that Shiny is working, or they will continuously change the parameters I provide in the side panel, which just causes Shiny to reactively restart the calculations once the initial run is completed.
>
> So, I created a conditional panel that shows a "Loading" message (referred to as a modal) with the following (thanks to Joe Cheng on the Shiny Google group for the conditional statement):
>
>     # generateButton is the name of my action button
>     loadPanel <- conditionalPanel("input.generateButton > 0 && $('html').hasClass('shiny-busy')"),
>                                   loadingMsg)
>
> This is working as intended if the user remains on the current tab. However, the user can switch to another tab (that may contain some calculations that need to be run for some time), but the loading panel appears and disappears immediately, all while R chugs away at the calculations, and then refreshing the content only after it is done.
>
> Since this may be hard to visualize, I provided some code to run below. You will notice that clicking the button to start the calculations will produce a nice loading message. However, when you switch to tab 2, R starts running some calculations, but fails to show the loading message (maybe Shiny does not register as being busy?). If you restart the calculations by pressing the button again, the loading screen will show up correctly.
>
> I want the loading message to appear when switching to a tab that is loading!
>
> ui.R
>
>     library(shiny)
>
>     # Code to make a message that shiny is loading
>     # Make the loading bar
>     loadingBar <- tags$div(class="progress progress-striped active",
>                            tags$div(class="bar", style="width: 100%;"))
>     # Code for loading message
>     loadingMsg <- tags$div(class="modal", tabindex="-1", role="dialog",
>                            "aria-labelledby"="myModalLabel", "aria-hidden"="true",
>                            tags$div(class="modal-header",
>                                     tags$h3(id="myModalHeader", "Loading...")),
>                            tags$div(class="modal-footer",

UI.r:

library(shiny)

library(shinyIncubator)

messages.body_plain:
We'll likely add support for arbitrary http request/response in the future, but only in the context of supporting Shiny applications, not as a substitute. Is there a reason you don't want to use Rook, RApache or FastRWeb for this? Those all seem like fine choices if what you want is servlet-like behavior.

No, it's just that I'm already using shiny. The scenario is that my main application is a node one, which carries a lot of tasks not always related to data analysis but which depends on R as a workhorse for all things data. Sometimes shiny is a fine fit but sometimes I need to expose the data in ways that the out-of-the-box shiny approach won't facilitate. In those cases I would like to completely decouple the data analysis from its presentation. If I could avoid running three web servers (node, shiny server and, say, rook) for this, I would be grateful.

Regards
--
Carlos

I think I got it...

Joe answered it here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/shiny-discuss/S15Vp7P72eg/yNv_O-axrd8J

Because my output was not being displayed, the calculation was suspended.

A line like this within the shinyServer function does the trick.

outputOptions(output, "csv_import_ready", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

This gist has been updated:  https://gist.github.com/ijlyttle/6230575

Thanks,

Ian

messages.subject_clean: R Shiny : Update graph/plot with fixed interval of time
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a plot in Shiny UI. If I change any input parameter and through reactivity plot will change. But let's consider following situation:- The plot in Shiny UI plotting let say intra-day price move of a stock. And for that you query some live data source. Now If I create a refresh button and then if time passes by I keep on clicking on refresh button. The plot will be updated as new data arrives as time goes into that live data source. Now my question is I don't want to keep clicking on refresh button. But I want to run a loop with timer so that it will check over a fixed interval of time and as soon as new data comes the plot will auto update. Something sort of Google Finance Graphs which keeps updating over time.

So the problem can be simplified as follows :- Let's consider this example from Shiny itself :- ui.R
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Hello Shiny!"),

  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("obs",
                "Number of observations:",
                min = 1,
                max = 1000,
                value = 500)
  ),

  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("distPlot")
  )
))

and server.R
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    # generate an rnorm distribution and plot it
    dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
    hist(dist)
  })

})

Now I want to generate a different random sample from normal distribution without any input activity. So basically I want to call
dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
hist(dist)

again without changing sliderInput. Please help me find out how to do that.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Lag Issue, Too Many Reactives?
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Lag Issue, Too Many Reactives?
messages.body_plain:
My problem was found- it isn't too many reactives, or even large amounts of data stored in reactives- it is the use of several conditional panels.  I had it set up so that there were 2 input fields (generated with renderUI, unsure if this is relevant) within each conditional panel.  I had two pages with a similar setup, I removed the conditional panel aspect from one (making their input fields always on display), and left the other as-is.  The lag only occurred after viewing the unchanged page with conditional panels in tact, the page without the conditional panels did not result in any issues.  I removed the conditional panels from both pages, and the lag is completely gone.  FWIW if you find that it takes a bit too long for your button clicks to respond, check if you have conditional panels on the page.

On Friday, August 16, 2013 2:09:58 PM UTC-4, Mike C wrote:
> Well, a surprisingly decent solution popped up, sprinkling gc() liberally throughout the code (just not the last line of the reactives and such), seems to have helped a lot.  I guess it can be chalked mostly up to R itself.
>

> > did the dropbox link not find the right home, to your @rstudio.com <http://rstudio.com> address?
> >
> > On Sunday, August 11, 2013 11:21:01 AM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > It's unlikely the number of reactives would slow things down--the overhead of reactive execution is fairly low and cost no CPU when they are not invalidated.
> > >
> > > Would it be possible to share your code?
> > >
> > > On Wednesday, August 7, 2013, Mike C wrote:
> > > > Hey all,
> > > >
> > > > I have been trying to make my app run more efficiently- because to my surprise, it can be a bit lagged on my 10gb mac desktop.  I investigated the memory usage on the machine after restarting, as the program ran and looked to see when it became sluggish responding to the user input.  I did not notice it ever having issues with ram, it almost always had at least 7gb free to work with, regardless of how sluggish it was/wasn't.
> > > >
> > > > I then decided to see which tabs it became sluggish after completing- I should probably describe the overall structure of my app.  The app is initially divided into many 6 tabs, all of which are page with sidebars.  The first tab is a initiation tab, where all the options are set for the analysis ahead, and after filling in all the fields, the analysis is run.  The five additional tabs are to generate and view figures and tables from the results of the analysis run on the first tab.  In the first tab, one of the fields is a 'select columns', not dissimilar from Winston's example.  This is the area in which I test the lag of checkbox clicking, initially, it is very rapid and keeps up with how fast I can click the buttons.
> > > >
> > > > The first tab has ~10 inputs, which are put into reactives and isolated by one of several action buttons.  After running the analysis itself, the checkboxes are only slightly more lagged, barely noticeable.
> > > > The second tab generates a simple plot, and there are only 3 inputs, which are put into reactives and isolated with an action button.  after generating a plot, there is no noticeable difference from the prior step.
> > > > The third tab and the fourth tab are similar, in that they have ~10 inputs each, which are turned into isolated reactives, and generate a plot and a table, respectively.  It is after generating either of these that the app becomes slow to respond to user input.
> > > > The fifth tab itself has only 2 inputs, each turned into an isolated reactive, but has 5 tabs, each of which have 3 tables.  There was no lag after generating these tables.
> > > > The sixth tab generates between 2 and 40 plots, but it is an optional analysis which takes a while to run, so I haven't tested it yet.
> > > >
> > > > So my question is, has anyone else experienced shiny being slow to respond to your input after generating ~20-30 reactives?  Or do you think it may be something else?
> > > >
> > > > Thanks again,
> > > > Mike

messages.body_plain:
I am quite newb and I haven't use the submit button much. I find action button a bit better.

Try actionButton in the ui.R in place of a submit button.

Say you name your actionButton myBtn then input$myBtn will increment by 1 everytime you press it. So now put everything that can the results into an isolate.

Eg.

observe({
  if(input$myBtn >0 ) {
     something <- isolate(input$someControl)
     dosomething(something)
  }
})

Make sure everything other than input$myBtn is wrapped in isolate.

messages.subject: Re: How do I include my own javascript files?
messages.subject_clean: How do I include my own javascript files?
messages.body_plain:
Do NOT put your own files into the www/shared folder! Your files will be deleted whenever you upgrade the Shiny package.

Instead, create a www directory in your own application folder, and copy the JS/CSS files there; for example, www/highcharts/js/highcharts.js will automatically be made available at the relative URL "highcharts/js/highcharts.js" (note the lack of "www" in the URL).

> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Since this may be hard to visualize, I provided some code to run below. You will notice that clicking the button to start the calculations will produce a nice loading message. However, when you switch to tab 2, R starts running some calculations, but fails to show the loading message (maybe Shiny does not register as being busy?). If you restart the calculations by pressing the button again, the loading screen will show up correctly.

> > > > > > > I want the loading message to appear when switching to a tab that is loading!
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > ui.R
> > > > > > >

> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >     # Code to make a message that shiny is loading

> > > > > > >                            "aria-labelledby"="myModalLabel", "aria-hidden"="true",
> > > > > > >                            tags$div(class="modal-header",
> > > > > > >                                     tags$h3(id="myModalHeader", "Loading...")),
> > > > > > >                            tags$div(class="modal-footer",
> > > > > > >                                     loadingBar))
> > > > > > >     # The conditional panel to show when shiny is busy
> > > > > > >     loadingPanel <- conditionalPanel(paste("input.goButton > 0 &&",
> > > > > > >                                            "$('html').hasClass('shiny-busy')"),
> > > > > > >                                      loadingMsg)
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >     # Now the UI code
> > > > > > >     shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
> > > > > > >       headerPanel("Tabsets"),
> > > > > > >       sidebarPanel(
> > > > > > >         sliderInput(inputId="time", label="System sleep time (in seconds)",
> > > > > > >                     value=1, min=1, max=5),
> > > > > > >         actionButton("goButton", "Let's go!")
> > > > > > >       ),
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >       mainPanel(
> > > > > > >         tabsetPanel(
> > > > > > >           tabPanel(title="Tab 1", loadingPanel, textOutput("tabText1")),
> > > > > > >           tabPanel(title="Tab 2", loadingPanel, textOutput("tabText2"))
> > > > > > >         )
> > > > > > >       )
> > > > > > >     ))
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > server.R
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >     library(shiny)
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >     # Define server logic for sleeping
> > > > > > >     shinyServer(function(input, output) {
> > > > > > >       sleep1 <- reactive({
> > > > > > >         if(input$goButton==0) return(NULL)
> > > > > > >         return(isolate({
> > > > > > >           Sys.sleep(input$time)
> > > > > > >           input$time
> > > > > > >         }))

> > > > > > >

> > > > > > >         if(input$goButton==0) return(NULL)
> > > > > > >         return(isolate({
> > > > > > >           Sys.sleep(input$time*2)
> > > > > > >           input$time*2
> > > > > > >         }))
> > > > > > >       })
> > > > > > >

messages.body_plain:
Hey guys, I understand the subset considerations inside Shiny from search through older posts but I'm having some difficulty figuring out the best way to subset a data frame on the fly with dynamically populated drop-downs ( something like options = as.list(levels(dat$Round)) )

This is a basic representation of what I have been doing for just selecting the data frame:

Global.R
Client1        <- read.csv("data/client1_audits.csv", header = TRUE, fill = FALSE)
Client2        <- read.csv("data/client1_audits.csv", header = TRUE, fill = FALSE)
Client3        <- read.csv("data/client3_audits.csv", header = TRUE, fill = FALSE)

data_sets <- c("Client1", "Client2", "Client3") #call from UI

Server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # get data from .csv defined in global.R
  inputVariable <- reactive({
    input$client_select
  })

  # ddply reactive
  reactive.auditorPlyr <- reactive({
    if(is.null(input$client_select))
      return()
    dat <- get(input$client_select)
    ddply(dat, .(Auditor), summarize,
          n            = length(Score),
          avgSco       = round(mean(Score),2),
          mScore       = round(median(Score),2),
          sdScore      = round(sd(Score),2),
          seScore      = round(sd(Score) / sqrt(length(Score)),2),
          avgDuration  = round(mean(Duration/60),2),
          mDuration    = round(median(Duration/60),2),
          sdDuration   = round(sd(Duration/60),2),
          seDuration   = round(sd(Duration/60) / sqrt(length(Duration/60)),2)
    )
  })

  output$auditorPlyr <- renderGvis({
    gvisTable(reactive.auditorPlyr() )
  })

UI.R

 sidebarPanel(

    wellPanel(
      selectInput("client_select", "Client:", as.list(data_sets)) # ,
      #selectInput("city_select", "City:", choices = as.list(levels(dat$City)))

      )

I'm creating the dataframe "dat" based off the single UI input from the globally defined csvs. What I would like to do is subset dat further via a few more drop downs that would fill based on the factors/levels of a column. For example a "city" dropdown would be populated by the entries that exist in the city column of the dataframe selected in dropdown 1 (client select). Then when a specific city is selected from the drop down the client dataframe is subsetted to only include observations where city == "xyz".

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: reactivity if/actionButton (bug?)
messages.subject_clean: reactivity if/actionButton (bug?)
messages.body_plain:
You're encountering a subtlety in how Shiny tracks dependencies between reactive components. The short version is that, in the first version of the code, after you click button1 so input$button1 is incremented, the renderText() returns before ever evaluating input$button2, so it stops tracking changes to input$button2.

What you want is for output$what_is_pressed to depend on input$button2. Each time the renderText for output$what_is_pressed runs, the reactive dependencies are cleared; as it runs the code and reaches another reactive component, it takes a dependency on that component. When it evaluates input$button1, the output object takes a dependency on input$button1 -- but then your code returns immediately (when button1_calls < input$button1) so it never reaches input$button2 and takes a dependency on that.

In summary, the dependency structure of the reactive components is cleared and created each time the code is executed -- Shiny doesn't scan the code ahead of time to track dependency structure.

See these sections of the tutorial for more information:
  http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview
  http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#execution-scheduling

-Winston

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

    values <- reactiveValues(lastPressed = NULL)

    observe({
        if (input$button1 > 0)
            values$lastPressed <- "Button 1"
    })

    observe({
        if (input$button2 > 0)
            values$lastPressed <- "Button 2"
    })

    output$what_is_pressed <- renderText({
        values$lastPressed
    })
})

messages.subject: Re: Expected checkboxGroupInput behavior?
messages.subject_clean: Expected checkboxGroupInput behavior?
messages.body_plain:
Seems to me like the roundControls needs to work on pre-filtered data, since you want to show the entire list of available rounds; while auditCounts wants to look at post-filtered data, i.e. just the selected rounds (if any).

In the below, clientData is pre-filtered and filteredClientData is post-filtered. I'm sure I messed something up in the actual filtering logic but hopefully the structure makes sense to you.

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  clientData <- reactive({
    if (is.null(input$client_select))
      return(NULL)
    get(input$client_select)
  })

  filteredClientData <- reactive({
    dat <- clientData()
    if (is.null(dat))
      return(NULL)
    if (!is.null(input$round_select))
      dat <- dat[dat$Round %in% input$round_select]
    return(dat)

  })

  # Dynamic UI experiment
  output$roundControls <- renderUI({

    if (is.null(clientData()))

      return("No client selected")

    checkboxGroupInput("round_select",
                       "Choose Round:",

                       as.character(levels(clientData$Round)),
                       selected = input$round_select)

  })

  # audit count
  output$auditsCount <- renderText({

    if (is.null(filteredClientData()))

      return("No client selected")

    paste("Total Audits:",nrow(filteredClientData()))
  })

messages.body_plain:
I assume you placed a browser() at the place where you want to debug the code.

I found that if you do this within a renderPrint it doesn't work as renderPrint "hijacks" the output to the console and redirects it to the webpage and it will show everything once the R finishes running.

For a quick fix, just change your renderPrint to renderUI while debugging and change it back once you are done.

messages.subject: Re: ConditionalPanel causing plot to load multiple times
messages.subject_clean: ConditionalPanel causing plot to load multiple times
messages.body_plain:
I suspect you might want to wrap all your controls in isolate in your server.R code e.g. isolate(input$something) where ever you have input$something in your server.R code. Also add a actionButton to the page and use if(input$yourActionButton >0 ) to run the code only if it's pressed. E.g.

output$something <- renderSomething({
if(input$yourActionButton > 0) {
  doSomethingWith(isloate(input$something))
  doSomethingWith(isloate(input$somethingElse))
}
})

instead of

output$something <- renderSomething({
  doSomethingWith(input$something)
  doSomethingWith1(input$somethingElse)
})

in the isolate example your output will not change until you press the yourActionButton, in the second cases whenever something or somethingElse changes your output will change

messages.subject: Re: Packages Rstudio server and Shiny server
messages.subject_clean: Packages Rstudio server and Shiny server
messages.body_plain:
If you set up Shiny Server as autouser/user_apps (see the configuration overview <http://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/config.html#overview>) then RStudio Server and Shiny Server will automatically share the same package library for each user. So each user can install packages using RStudio Server and they will be available to their own Shiny apps. This is how we run glimmer.rstudio.com <http://glimmer.rstudio.com>.

You as the superuser can also install libraries in the system-wide R library, which will again be available to both RStudio and Shiny. To do this, run "sudo su - R" and install whatever packages you want from that R prompt, and they should be installed in the system-wide library.

On Tue, Aug 20, 2013 at 7:19 AM, Brent Sitterly <sitt...@gmail.com> wrote:

> What are best practices for managing packages for a Shiny server and an Rstudio server, that reside on the same machine?
>
> I currently have one Centos VM that is both an RStudio server and a Shiny server.  I ramping it up to be a resource for my group.  Is anyone doing the same thing?  Are you leaving the packages up to each individual "R developer" to install and manage?  Or does it makes sense to configure both servers to look at the same set of libraries and have a centralized package management process?  Based on the what we'll be using it for I am leaning towards the latter.
>
> That being said, how do you set this Linux box up so that there is only one list of packages that both Rstudio and Shiny use?
>
> Thanks for any suggestions.
>
> Brent

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Many thanks,
Jack

I had identical problems. For others having this problem -- what got the examples showing up for me were these things..
when installing shiny-server, making sure it installed as a global package i.e. including the -g when doing sudo npm install -g shiny-server
making sure inbound TCP connections through port 3838 (if thats what you're using) are allowed:
sudo ufw allow 3838/tcp
As a newbie myself, I can't really speak to why those worked for me but after tripping and falling around with the same problems above that was what eventually worked... good luck!
