messages.body_plain:
No I didn't succeed that way.

Finally, I think the best way in the long run is to play with session variables. Which I didn't tried out yet.

For the moment I opted for a temporary solution: a text field and two buttons: "lock" and "unlock". A passphrase is defined on the server side. This key must be entered in the text field and "unlock" sends the value to the server. If the key is correct, all the rest of the application is made visible to the user.

Now the trick is that, if you define the rest of the application -which is supposed to be protected- on the client side within a simple conditionalPanel(), your protection will be very poor: the supposedly protected content is merely "hidden" by javascript/css, but still accessible from the source code of the page. So you have to define all the protected content on the server side, and use a renderUI() on server side, coupled with a uiOutput() on client side.

Finally, almost everything is defined on server side, and almost nothing on the client side, except for the lock/unlock panel.

messages.body_plain:
Yes, you must compile the code on the server (or a very similar environment, i.e. the same Linux distribution/version). You could use Tools | Shell from within RStudio Server to drop to something (badly) approximating a shell prompt, and manually call make/g++/whatever from there.

The better long-term solution though, is to put your C++ code (and the rest of your analysis?) in a package, with or without Rcpp. Not only is R well designed to compile and/or distribute native code this way, but RStudio will do the compilation and installation for you when you do "Build and Reload" on the Build pane (only available if your current project is an R package).

Here's Hadley's take on the Rcpp way of doing things (in particular, note "Using Rcpp in a Package"):
http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Rcpp.html

> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > I am working on making a web app with Shiny, and some of the R commands that I am executing take minutes to complete. > > > > > > > > Since this may be hard to visualize, I provided some code to run below. You will notice that clicking the button to start the calculations will produce a nice loading message. > > > > > > > > I want the loading message to appear when switching to a tab that is loading!
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > ui.R
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >     library(shiny)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >     # Code to make a message that shiny is loading
> > > > > > > >     # Make the loading bar

> > > > > > > >                            tags$div(class="bar", style="width: 100%;"))
> > > > > > > >     # Code for loading message
> > > > > > > >     loadingMsg <- tags$div(class="modal", tabindex="-1", role="dialog",
> > > > > > > >                            "aria-labelledby"="myModalLabel", "aria-hidden"="true",
> > > > > > > >                            tags$div(class="modal-header",
> > > > > > > >                                     tags$h3(id="myModalHeader", "Loading...")),
> > > > > > > >                            tags$div(class="modal-footer",
> > > > > > > >                                     loadingBar))
> > > > > > > >     # The conditional panel to show when shiny is busy
> > > > > > > >     loadingPanel <- conditionalPanel(paste("input.goButton > 0 &&",
> > > > > > > >                                            "$('html').hasClass('shiny-busy')"),
> > > > > > > >                                      loadingMsg)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >     # Now the UI code
> > > > > > > >     shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
> > > > > > > >       headerPanel("Tabsets"),
> > > > > > > >       sidebarPanel(
> > > > > > > >         sliderInput(inputId="time", label="System sleep time (in seconds)",
> > > > > > > >                     value=1, min=1, max=5),
> > > > > > > >         actionButton("goButton", "Let's go!")
> > > > > > > >       ),
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >       mainPanel(
> > > > > > > >         tabsetPanel(
> > > > > > > >           tabPanel(title="Tab 1", loadingPanel, textOutput("tabText1")),
> > > > > > > >           tabPanel(title="Tab 2", loadingPanel, textOutput("tabText2"))
> > > > > > > >         )
> > > > > > > >       )
> > > > > > > >     ))
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > server.R
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >     library(shiny)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >     # Define server logic for sleeping
> > > > > > > >     shinyServer(function(input, output) {
> > > > > > > >       sleep1 <- reactive({
> > > > > > > >         if(input$goButton==0) return(NULL)
> > > > > > > >         return(isolate({
> > > > > > > >           Sys.sleep(input$time)
> > > > > > > >           input$time
> > > > > > > >         }))
> > > > > > > >       })
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >       sleep2 <- reactive({
> > > > > > > >         if(input$goButton==0) return(NULL)
> > > > > > > >         return(isolate({
> > > > > > > >           Sys.sleep(input$time*2)
> > > > > > > >           input$time*2
> > > > > > > >         }))
> > > > > > > >       })
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >       output$tabText1 <- renderText({
> > > > > > > >         if(input$goButton==0) return(NULL)
> > > > > > > >         return({
> > > > > > > >           print(paste("Slept for", sleep1(), "seconds."))
> > > > > > > >         })
> > > > > > > >       })
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >       output$tabText2 <- renderText({
> > > > > > > >         if(input$goButton==0) return(NULL)
> > > > > > > >         return({
> > > > > > > >           print(paste("Multiplied by 2, that is", sleep2(), "seconds."))
> > > > > > > >         })
> > > > > > > >       })
> > > > > > > >     })

shiny 0.6.0 is the most recent version we have on CRAN, but we develop shiny on GitHub, so you can always get the latest version here: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny

The easiest way to install the latest version of Shiny is to use the devtools package:

# install.packages("devtools") #(if you don't already have it installed)
library(devtools)
install_github("shiny", "rstudio')

At that point, you should be able to get shinyDash to install and run.

Jeff

Hello. I'm trying to slightly alter the actionbutton input binding object to fit my needs. There is three buttons (lets say b1,b2 and execute).b1 and b2 represents choices while execute button do some processing after user clicks either b1 or b2. So i set all buttons to actionbutton class and everything works really nice. But if i want to count how many times user has pressed b1 or b2 there is a possible error. Because they are action buttons they do +1 at each click. I would like to set b1 and b2 to another custom input binding class that will behave as following: cutom input binding class is triggered by pressing execute button and checking if b1 is clicked. Then value of b1 can be +1 and not any time you press b1. or let's say we want to add +1 to the last pressed button before execute button is pressed.

Reading tutorials with custom input binding didn't give solution while not being "pro" in JQuery

Super thanks in advance for any thought

This question should be equal to many user questions of how you can add a js variable in shiny and finally in R. I set this question to the forum with the hope of expressing many other people with same problems.And I clearly think that custom inputbinding is the key for shiny's booming.

  # Get main dataframe clientData

  clientData <- reactive({
    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(input$client_select))
      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>(NULL)
    get <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/get>(input$client_select)
  })

  # Filter clientData based on Service

    dat <- clientData()
    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(dat))
      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>(NULL)

    if (!is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(input$service_select)) # NOT is.null
      dat <- dat[dat$Service.Name %in% input$service_select,]
    return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>(dat)
  })

    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(clientData()))
      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>("No client selected")

                       "Choose Round:",

                       choices = as.character <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/as.character>(levels <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/levels>(roundFiltered_clientData()$Round)))

  # Audit count panel

    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(roundFiltered_clientData()))

    paste <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/paste>("Total Audits:",nrow <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/nrow>(roundFiltered_clientData()))

messages.body_plain:
Wondering about the same thing and Kenny's is a great suggestion.  Has RStudio team responded to this suggestion?

On Saturday, April 20, 2013 1:34:05 PM UTC-7, Kenny Darrell wrote:
> I have been making an r package that uses shiny interfaces as demos and they work great. The one problem I have is that there seems to be some hoops I have to jump through if I want more that one demo. For instance I cannot have multiple server.R and ui.R files in the demo directory. I can have multiple files called from demo that can run multiple interactive shiny demos, but they have to jump through hoops to point to the correct server and ui files. It also gets rather difficult to track multiple files with the same name. I investigated the source code and it seems the runApp() function I use calls the startApp() function. This has two lines that set the server.R and ui.R files.
> uiR <- file.path.ci <http://file.path.ci>(getwd(), 'ui.R')
> serverR <- file.path.ci <http://file.path.ci>(getwd(), 'server.R')
> Is there a reason that these are hard-coded to these names. Would it be more robust if you could pass runApp() two arguments which would also be passed to startApp(). They could be defaulted by runApp(ui = 'ui.R', server = 'server.R') if you give it the directory, but you can then have more flexibility by being able to call runApp(appDir = 'dir') directory or runApp(ui = MY'ui.R', server = 'MYserver.R'). Or it would even open the door to using an actual function as an argument. Since server.R consists of a shinyServer() which wraps a function you could pass the function as an argument, you could have logic before hand that could modify the function based on the circumstances. This could give different interfaces based on the data or other parameters involved.

On Saturday, April 20, 2013 4:34:05 PM UTC-4, Kenny Darrell wrote:
> I have been making an r package that uses shiny interfaces as demos and they work great. The one problem I have is that there seems to be some hoops I have to jump through if I want more that one demo. For instance I cannot have multiple server.R and ui.R files in the demo directory. I can have multiple files called from demo that can run multiple interactive shiny demos, but they have to jump through hoops to point to the correct server and ui files. It also gets rather difficult to track multiple files with the same name. I investigated the source code and it seems the runApp() function I use calls the startApp() function. This has two lines that set the server.R and ui.R files.
> uiR <- file.path.ci <http://file.path.ci>(getwd(), 'ui.R')
> serverR <- file.path.ci <http://file.path.ci>(getwd(), 'server.R')
> Is there a reason that these are hard-coded to these names. Would it be more robust if you could pass runApp() two arguments which would also be passed to startApp(). They could be defaulted by runApp(ui = 'ui.R', server = 'server.R') if you give it the directory, but you can then have more flexibility by being able to call runApp(appDir = 'dir') directory or runApp(ui = MY'ui.R', server = 'MYserver.R'). Or it would even open the door to using an actual function as an argument. Since server.R consists of a shinyServer() which wraps a function you could pass the function as an argument, you could have logic before hand that could modify the function based on the circumstances. This could give different interfaces based on the data or other parameters involved.

messages.subject: Shiny 0.7.0 released
messages.subject_clean: Shiny 0.7.0 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

Shiny 0.7.0 has been released to CRAN, and should get to your local mirror in the next day or two. Here are some of the highlights from the NEWS file:

* The `input` and `output` objects are now also accessible via `session$input`
  and `session$output`.

* Added click and hover events for static plots; see `?plotOutput` for details.

* Reactive expressions now have class="reactive" attribute. Also added
  `is.reactive()` and `is.reactivevalues()` functions.

* New `stopApp()` function, which stops an app and returns a value to the caller
  of `runApp()`.

* Added the `shiny.usecairo` option, which can be used to tell Shiny not to use
  Cairo for PNG output even when it is installed. (Defaults to `TRUE`.)

* The HTTP request object that created the websocket is now accessible from the
  `session` object, as `session$request`. This is a Rook-like request
  environment that can be used to access HTTP headers, among other things.
  (Note: When running in a Shiny Server environment, the request will reflect
  the proxy HTTP request that was made from the Shiny Server process to the R
  process, not the request that was made from the web browser to Shiny Server.)

* Fix `getComputedStyle` issue, for IE8 browser compatibility (#196). Note:
  Shiny Server is still required for IE8/9 compatibility.

For the full list of changes, see:
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shiny/NEWS

We will also be upgrading Shiny to 0.7.0 on our beta hosting servers, Glimmer and Spark, at the end of this week.

Enjoy!
-Winston

Hello everyone,

I have various renderTable functions that fail if certain conditions are not met, and it fills my shiny app with annoying error messages. I would like to get rid of the red Error messages and send an information message instead by adding something like this to the functions:

if( failing condition) {
 return("Explanation")
}

It seems so simple, but still, I can't seem to get it.

return("Explanation message")         # creates an error because xtable does not handle character vectors.

warning("Explanation")                   # The explanation is only displayed in the console, not in the browser.

stop("Explanation")                      # Back to square one: I can choose the message, but it still shows as an error.

Anyone has a clever idea?

Thanks

Frederic

messages.subject_clean: Package location with user_apps
messages.body_plain:
Hi Josh,

I know there have been questions about this before, but I can't get it to work.

I'm using RStudio (versions/system below) with a new install of Shiny today. RStudio and Shiny are working great. This is on Amazon EC2.

I'm trying to run a shiny app from a user account. I have /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf as:
run_as shiny;

server {
  listen 3838;

  location / {
    site_dir /var/shiny-server/www;
    log_dir /var/shiny-server/log;
    directory_index on;
  }

  location / {
    user_apps on;
  }
}

This is working fine and I can see my app at http://<server>:3838/<user>/<app>/

The problem is making packages available to this. The user packages aren't available as it is being run as user = shiny. I've tried various permutations of added paths including in rserver.config without success. I've even (and I know I shouldn't probably do this) made "shiny" a normal user and added the packages to that account, but that still doesn't work.

Would it be possible to have an option that when user_apps = on, the packages for that user are available to shiny?

Is there a line I can add some where to make this happen? I'm not that au fait with linux paths and all the jazz.

Error is:
> An error has occurred
>
> The application failed to start.
>
> The application exited during initialization.
>
> Error in library(ggplot2) : there is no package called ‘ggplot2’ Calls: runApp ... eval -> source -> withVisible -> eval -> eval -> library Execution halted

Did you say some where else that ggplot2 had been added to a system library? I can't find it.

Many thanks!

Ewen

messages.subject: Re: Sending information message from renderTable if some condition is not met
messages.subject_clean: Sending information message from renderTable if some condition is not met
messages.body_plain:
That's a really bad idea, I wouldn't do that. It only happens to work today by coincidence (that the tableOutput and textOutput bindings are similar-ish), and we're almost guaranteed to break you in the future as we enhance renderTable/tableOutput.

How about if you use an htmlOutput/renderText, and if you're rendering a table, manually call xtable?

  tableAsHTML <- function(data) {
    require('xtable')
    classNames <- 'data table table-bordered table-condensed'

    if (is.null(data) || identical(data, data.frame()))
      return("")

    return(paste(
      capture.output(
        print(xtable(data, ...),
              type='html',
              html.table.attributes=paste('class="',
                                          htmlEscape(classNames, TRUE),
                                          '"',
                                          sep=''), ...)),
      collapse="\n"))
  }

On Wed, Aug 28, 2013 at 7:40 AM, <frederic...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thank you Ramnath and Joe!
>
> Ramnath solution is a good one for one table. But I would find difficult to use it for many tables with many possible warning messages.
>
> Joe's solution works well for hiding the fact that errors are thrown (which was indeed something I wanted to do!), but it still relies on throwing an error. This might cause problems at some point, and it still fills the console with error messages.
>
> The solution that I've just found is simply to use a renderText to return the message, and then return NULL to the renderTable function and it's xtable machinery.
>
> output$myTable <- renderTable({
>     if( failing condition) {
>         output$myTable <-renderText ({"Explanation message"})
>         return (NULL)
>     }
> ...
> })
>
> I was concerned about having two different 'render' for a same output, and about using a 'renderText' for a 'tableOuput', but so far it seems to work...
> Joe, do you think that I'll shoot myself in the foot by doing this?
>
> Thanks for your help!

Hi Thibault, Thank you for your quick reply and explanation of your approach! I applied your suggested rendering approach and it's working.

In rolling on with this "temporary" solution, I was wondering if you would recommend taking any further security steps in protecting data on the server side? I have little experience in this realm, so I'd greatly appreciate any suggestions or terms or concepts I should look up.

Again, thanks!

On Friday, 23 August 2013 03:23:37 UTC-4, Thibault Helleputte wrote:
> No I didn't succeed that way.
>
> Finally, I think the best way in the long run is to play with session variables. Which I didn't tried out yet.
>
> For the moment I opted for a temporary solution: a text field and two buttons: "lock" and "unlock". A passphrase is defined on the server side. This key must be entered in the text field and "unlock" sends the value to the server. If the key is correct, all the rest of the application is made visible to the user.
>
> Now the trick is that, if you define the rest of the application -which is supposed to be protected- on the client side within a simple conditionalPanel(), your protection will be very poor: the supposedly protected content is merely "hidden" by javascript/css, but still accessible from the source code of the page. So you have to define all the protected content on the server side, and use a renderUI() on server side, coupled with a uiOutput() on client side.
>
> Finally, almost everything is defined on server side, and almost nothing on the client side, except for the lock/unlock panel.
>
>

messages.subject: Re: traceback in errors
messages.subject_clean: traceback in errors
messages.body_plain:
Looks like a few people have run into this issue too.
The alternative proposed here: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2004-March/047653.html seems to catch errors successfully (although I found it somewhat useful to modify try myTry logic to cat the traceback rather than return it).

myTry <- function(expr) {
  withRestarts(
    withCallingHandlers(expr,
                        error = function(e) {
                          error  = e
                          calls  = sys.calls()
                          frames = sys.frames()
                          invokeRestart("myAbort", e, calls, frames)
                        }),
    myAbort = function(e, calls, frames){
      err = list(error = e, calls=calls, frames=frames)
      cat(as.character(err$error), '\n')
      lapply(err$calls, function(x) cat(as.character(x), '\n', file = stderr() ))
      stop()
    }
  )
}

## Example of use
f <- function(x) x + 2
g <- function(...) f(...)
myTry({g(2)})
# Returns 4

myTry({g('dog')})
# Prints the call stack, although it'd probably make sense to filter out the less readable levels, like withRestarts, etc.

However, if you absolutely have to, you can use pdf.js plugin or google drive.
Worked with google viewer:
1. Upload pdf on google drive (theoretically should work with any repository, but I haven't tried).
2. Set the sharing to everyone on the web (viewer seems to give an error otherwise).
3. Inside google drive click on uploaded file, then on the bottom click on Open button.
4. Go to File/Embed this PDF File.
5. Copy code from opened window.
6. Paste it inside UI.R in relevant tabPanel in HTML('code').
7. Don't forget to add escape \ character before every inner quotation marks.
here's an example:
                ,tabPanel
                (
                    "Help",
                    HTML('<iframe src=\"https://docs.google.com/file/d/0B3slTsWp_oiBYUxIb01xTWFlemM/preview\ <https://docs.google.com/file/d/0B3slTsWp_oiBYUxIb01xTWFlemM/preview%5C>"
                         width=\"900\" height=\"600\"></iframe>')
                )

messages.subject: To capture the name of the data set selected by the user?
messages.subject_clean: To capture the name of the data set selected by the user?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks in advance.

I am using R-3.0.1 on Windows XP.

May I request you for the following please.

I am trying to use googleVis with shiny.

I am using the example given in the section 3.4.4 of "Using the Google Chart Tools with R: googleVis-0.4.3 Package Vignette" document. The code is below.

It is working fine.

In this example, user can select the data set to be displayed.

I like to give a title for the chart.

In server.R:

gvisScatterChart(datasetInput(), options= list(title= ???))

The question is:

- How can I capture the name of the data set selected by the user?

x <- ???

I like to capture the name of the data set in x.

I like to give a good title of the graph using x. example: titleName = paste(x, ": Test only"). This is the title, I like to give.

Once again, thank you very much for the time you have given.

Regards,

Deb

# server.R

library(shiny)

library(googleVis)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

datasetInput <- reactive({

switch(input$dataset,

"rock" = rock,

"pressure" = pressure,

"cars" = cars)

})

x <- datasetInput

print(x)

output$view <- renderGvis({

gvisScatterChart(datasetInput())

})

})

# ui.R

library(shiny)

library(googleVis)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

headerPanel("googleVis on Shiny"),

sidebarPanel(

selectInput("dataset", "Choose a dataset:",

choices = c("rock", "pressure", "cars"))

),

mainPanel(

htmlOutput("view")

)

))

      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>("No client selected")
    selectInput("service_select",
                "Choose Service:",
                choices = as.character <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/as.character>(levels <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/levels>(clientData()$Service.Name)),
                selected = input$service_select
    )
  })

  # Second UI input (Rounds column) filter service-filtered clientData

  output$roundControls <- renderUI({
    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(serviceFiltered_clientData()))
      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>("No service selected")
    checkboxGroupInput("round_select",
                       "Choose Round:",

                       choices = as.character <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/as.character>(levels <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/levels>(serviceFiltered_clientData()$Round)))
  })

  # First data load (client data)

  clientData <- reactive({
    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(input$client_select))
      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>(NULL)
    get <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/get>(input$client_select)
  })

  # Second data load (filter by service column)

  serviceFiltered_clientData <- reactive({
    dat <- clientData()
    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(dat))
      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>(NULL)

    if (!is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(input$service_select)) # !

      dat <- dat[dat$Service.Name %in% input$service_select,]
    return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>(dat)
  })

  # Third data load (filter by service column)

  roundFiltered_clientData <- reactive({
    dat <- serviceFiltered_clientData()
    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(dat))
      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>(NULL)

    if (!is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(input$round_select)) # !

      dat <- dat[dat$Round %in% input$round_select,]
    return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>(dat)
  })

# Audit count panel
  output$auditsCount <- renderText({
    if (is.null <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/is.null>(roundFiltered_clientData()))
      return <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/return>("No client selected")
    paste <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/paste>("Total Audits:",nrow <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/nrow>(roundFiltered_clientData()))
  })

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to display a word or pdf file in a panel?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to display a word or pdf file in a panel?
messages.body_plain:
Joe, this would require pdf plugin installed in a browser to show correctly. Most browsers have it though.

To guarantee the work on all platforms you should either include js viewer like pdf.js in your Shiny project or use an online viewer like the one I mentioned (works for word docs as well)

messages.body_plain:
This question is somewhat related to the password question in this thread:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/BerC7XCeRD0/TnNaZlvPKt4J

I would like to use Shiny to allow the user to connect to an external data-source.

This data-source may provide a hierarchical list from which the user may wish to make a selection.

I would imagine that such an input could be expressed in R using nested lists, i.e.:

nested_list <- list(
  Canada = list(
    Edmonton = "e123",
    Calgary = "c456"
  ),
  USA = list(
    Seattle = "s789",
    Boston = "b012"
  )
)

In essence, it would be a more-complicated version of selectInput().

Is there, or could there be a way to do this?

Thanks,

Ian

messages.body_plain:
If you know the maximum number of levels your list can have (say n), you can create n controls with renderUI and check if the deeper level is list or not. Something like this
ui.R
....
  sidebarPanel(
    uiOutput("sel1"),
    uiOutput("sel2"),
    uiOutput("sel3")
  ),

server.R
library(shiny)
# list with inconsistent number of levels (max 3)
data = list(a = "a", b = list(ba = "ba", bb = "bb"), c = list(ca ="ca", cb = list(cba = "cba", cbb = "cbb")))
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    output$sel1 = renderUI(selectInput("sel1", "first", choices=names(data)))

    output$sel2 = renderUI({if (is.list(data[[input$sel1]]))
                               selectInput("sel2", "second", choices = names(data[[input$sel1]]))
    })
    output$sel3 = renderUI({if (!is.null(input$sel1) &&
                                !is.null(input$sel2) &&
                                is.list(data[[input$sel1]] [[input$sel2]]))
                                selectInput("sel2", "third", choices = data[[input$sel1]][[input$sel2]])
    })
})

Ugly, but I don't see any better solution. Also, when you don't know the maximum number of levels, it gets tricky: I don't think any recursion is possible inside renderUI.
It's an interesting question.
